questionText:
Select the option that corrects the following sentence.
He has broken his leg yesterday.
questionTextHi:
Select the option that corrects the following sentence.
He has broken his leg yesterday.

options.text: He has broke his leg yesterday.
options.textHi: He has broke his leg yesterday.

options.text: He had broke his leg yesterday.
options.textHi: He had broke his leg yesterday.

options.text: He have broken his leg yesterday.
options.textHi: He have broken his leg yesterday.

explanation: The past time adverb 'yesterday' specifies a definite completed past action, which requires Simple Past Tense (V2) rather than Present Perfect. The V2 form of 'break' is 'broke'. Hence, 'He broke his leg yesterday' is grammatically correct.

subject: english
questionText:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
I goes to / attend dance classes at / the National Dance Academy.
questionTextHi:
The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
I goes to / attend dance classes at / the National Dance Academy.
explanation: The first-person singular pronoun 'I' takes the base form of the verb 'go', not the third-person singular form 'goes'. Therefore, 'I goes to' is grammatically incorrect and should be corrected to 'I go to'.
explanationHi: The first-person singular pronoun 'I' takes the base form of the verb 'go', not the third-person singular form 'goes'. Therefore, 'I goes to' is grammatically incorrect and should be corrected to 'I go to'.
source: SSC CHSL Tier-I PYQ · CHSL Tier-I (02 July 2024) Shift- 2

subject: english
questionText:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
I noticed that they / did not went to / the museum but entered / a shopping complex.
questionTextHi:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
I noticed that they / did not went to / the museum but entered / a shopping complex.
explanation: The auxiliary verb 'did' is always followed by the base form of the verb (V1). Using the past tense form 'went' with 'did' is an error of double past. It should be 'did not go to'.
explanationHi: The auxiliary verb 'did' is always followed by the base form of the verb (V1). Using the past tense form 'went' with 'did' is an error of double past. It should be 'did not go to'.
source: SSC CHSL Tier-I PYQ · CHSL Tier-I (02 July 2024) Shift- 2
